chunks: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He was asked about a man who paid dirhams in advance for five measures of wheat or barley until a specified term. When the one who owed the wheat or barley was unable to pay all that had become due, and the صاحب of the right wished to take half of the food, or a third of it, or less than that, or more, and take the principal value of what remained of the food in dirhams, he said: There is no harm in it.

He said: And he was asked about saffron, in which a man advances dirhams for twenty mithqāls, or less than that, or more. He said: There is no harm if the one who owes the saffron is unable to give him all that is due from him, that he take half of his due, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and take the principal value of what remains of his due in dirhams.

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: a fixed, specified term for delivery
key_terms.أَسْلَمَ: paid in advance in a salam transaction
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: it is legally unobjectionable or permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in a salam sale to take part of the goods and the rest of the principal back in dirhams if the seller cannot fully deliver?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salam transactions in which payment is made in advance for specified goods to be delivered later. If the seller cannot deliver the full amount when due, it is permissible for the buyer to accept part of the goods and recover the remaining principal value in dirhams.
